evals.prompt: design a terraform module for our vpc setup
evals.expected_output: Bases the interface on comparing at least two or three real call sites rather than guessing, gives every variable a description and sane default with input validation, exposes only the outputs callers need, and pins the module to an exact version/tag.

evals.prompt: every time someone bumps a module we get surprise breakage
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses an unpinned module source floating on a branch or unpinned registry version, and fixes it by pinning to an exact version or Git tag with deliberate, changelog-reviewed bumps instead of implicit upgrades via terraform init -upgrade.

evals.prompt: i wrote a module after the very first vpc config so we can reuse it right away
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: extracting from a single use case bakes in that example's assumptions as general requirements; wait for a third real repetition so the varying parts of the interface are actually known before building the abstraction.
